text.p: Bonds closed firmer but in fairly thin business with Monday likely to be even quieter because of the Tuesday Carnaval holiday, traders said.
"We closed higher with Europe, after the Treasuries rallied with the (U.S.) jobs data, but the liquidity was low," said one fixed-income trader.

"Despite the gains, the spread for the 10-year (Portuguese bond) OT, and the (Spanish) Bonos, is probably capped at around 100 basis points," said another trader, referring to the spread with the German Bunds.
Traders said that the G7 meeting at the weekend was not expected to announce anything that might weaken the dollar and therefore hurt periphery markets.

But the shorter end of the curve could suffer slightly from nervousness about Portugal's inflation even if analysts say that a predicted upturn in the year-on-year rate in January will be entirely due to statistical factors.
